question: Supplier S-104 will miss its next ship date. Handle it.
answer:
I worked through the full disruption process for S-104. There is no qualified backup supplier, so I split the remaining Lacrivia stock at DC-EAST among the three top-tier contract health systems (approved), notified all 23 affected accounts, and passed the wholesaler notice to Trade Relations.

**What I found**
- **The late order:** S-104 (Delmar Specialty Chemicals) has three open orders. The next one is **PO005791**: 4,200 units of RM-221 (Polysorbate 80), promised to ship 2026-10-07. PO000369 (more RM-221, promised 2026-10-29) and PO000430 (RM-222, promised 2026-10-26) are also open.
- **No backup supplier:** S-104 is the only qualified source for RM-221. The other listed supplier, S-131, is not qualified and not approved in the supplier portal. So I raised no purchase requisition. The emulsifier premix made from RM-221 (CMP-310) is also single-source, from S-201.
- **Products affected:** RM-221 goes into Lacrivia 0.1% 5 mL and 10 mL and Cyclosporine OS 0.05% 5 mL. It also goes into 11 lens-care products, FG-3001 to FG-3011.
- **Stock vs safety stock (snapshot 2026-09-25):**

| Product | DC | On hand | Safety stock | Below? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lacrivia 5 mL (99101010105) | DC-EAST | 46 | 471 | Yes |
| Lacrivia 10 mL (99101010110) | DC-EAST | 34 | 233 | Yes |

  DC-CENTRAL and DC-WEST are above safety stock for every affected product. Cyclosporine OS is above safety stock at all three DCs.
- **No substitute to offer:** the other Lacrivia pack is also short at DC-EAST, and Cyclosporine OS (the approved substitute) uses the same material. Medical Affairs guides therapeutic alternatives.
- **Recovery:** finished goods reach the DC 50 days after RM-221 ships, including the 14-day sterility test. That means DC-EAST recovers no earlier than about 2026-11-26, and later depending on how late S-104 ships.

**Actions taken**
1. **Approval APR-19080A49 – approved.** The DC-EAST plan is 80 units worth $45,840 at list price, which is over the $25,000 approval threshold.
2. **Allocations recorded, both under that approval.** Units went to the three Tier A contract health systems, split by their last-13-week prescriptions (TRx) of each pack from prescribers in DC-EAST's states. Nothing was left for Tier B or other accounts.

   | Account | 5 mL (AL-0140CB7B, 46 units) | 10 mL (AL-47FBF1BF, 34 units) |
   |---|---|---|
   | Riverbend (AC00059) | 20 | 15 |
   | Oak Hollow (AC00038) | 15 | 11 |
   | Northfield (AC00117) | 11 | 8 |

3. **Account team tasks in the CRM (23):** each says what the account was allocated (or that it got none), the expected recovery date and that there is no substitute.
   - With an allocation: CRM-532B704D (Riverbend), CRM-37F0B482 (Oak Hollow), CRM-99F6572F (Northfield).
   - Tier B, no allocation: CRM-38535EEA (Clearview), CRM-A45FF4FC (Sunridge).
   - Other accounts, no allocation: CRM-2015E4AD, CRM-F05F3567, CRM-14628AAC, CRM-B16E00F4, CRM-182CA581, CRM-AB1617AE, CRM-CA025281, CRM-9B3A7166, CRM-F2334153, CRM-5A554443, CRM-F72C646A, CRM-9984A16D, CRM-D6F85E8C, CRM-24635C61, CRM-1CF8C41A, CRM-40409E39, CRM-50FA5119, CRM-A586D8A9.
4. **CASE-91319439 → Trade Relations:** notify the two wholesalers DC-EAST ships Lacrivia to, Keystone (W-01) and Atlas (W-02). The wholesaler EDI gateway has no API, so the process hands this to Trade Relations.
5. **CASE-0CE6A624 → Supply Planning:**
   - The 11 lens-care products fed by RM-221 have no DC stock or demand data in the governed data, so I couldn't check or allocate them.
   - It also flags the two later S-104 orders. RM-222 has a qualified, active backup supplier, S-130, approved for plant PL-02.
   - It recommends qualifying a second source for RM-221.

**What I did not do, and why**
- **No purchase requisition:** there is no qualified, approved backup supplier for RM-221.
- **No allocation at DC-CENTRAL or DC-WEST, or for Cyclosporine OS:** none of these is below safety stock.
- **No stock transfer between DCs:** the process doesn't call for one. The supply planning lead could move stock from DC-CENTRAL or DC-WEST (Lacrivia 5 mL is at 677 and 593 units) to DC-EAST, which would need separate approval.
- **No wholesaler inventory check:** that feed isn't live until Q4 2026.
- **No action on RM-222:** its order isn't the one at risk now.
- **No case opened for Medical Affairs:** the account notices just tell accounts that Medical Affairs will advise on alternatives.

**Assumptions**
- "Next ship date" means PO005791.
- Each prescriber is placed in a state by the state of the account they belong to.
- Accounts are rolled up to their top-level parent (at most three levels deep).
- "Last 13 weeks" means the 13 most recent weeks in the prescription data.

**Knowledge-layer sources**
- Process: Supply Disruption Response, steps SDR-1.1 to SDR-4.2.
- Rules: BR-ALLOC-01 and -02, BR-APPR-01, BR-SUB-01 and -02, BR-LEAD-01, BR-CUST-01, BR-REGION-01, POL-DUA-01 (I used no patient-level data).
- Reference sets: supply_contracts, list_prices, dc_service_regions, approved_substitutes.
- Tools: trace_supply_exposure and get_lead_times.
- No trusted playbook matched this situation.

sql.sql: SELECT p.PO_ID, p.SUPPLIER_ID, s.SUPPLIER_NM, s.TIER, p.MATERIAL_ID, p.ORDER_DT, p.PROMISED_SHIP_DT, p.ACTUAL_SHIP_DT, p.QTY, p.STATUS FROM dbo.PURCH_ORD p JOIN dbo.SUPPLIER s ON s.SUPPLIER_ID=p.SUPPLIER_ID WHERE p.SUPPLIER_ID='S-104' AND p.STATUS='OPEN' ORDER BY p.PROMISED_SHIP_DT

SELECT sm.SUPPLIER_ID, sm.MATERIAL_ID, sm.QUALIFIED_FLG, sm.PRIMARY_FLG, s.TIER FROM dbo.SUPPLIER_MATERIAL sm JOIN dbo.SUPPLIER s ON s.SUPPLIER_ID=sm.SUPPLIER_ID WHERE sm.MATERIAL_ID IN (SELECT MATERIAL_ID FROM dbo.SUPPLIER_MATERIAL WHERE SUPPLIER_ID='S-104')

SELECT i.DC_ID, i.MATERIAL_ID, i.SNAPSHOT_DT, i.ON_HAND_UNITS, i.SAFETY_STOCK_UNITS, CASE WHEN i.ON_HAND_UNITS < i.SAFETY_STOCK_UNITS THEN 'BELOW' ELSE 'OK' END AS STATUS FROM dbo.DC_INV i WHERE i.SNAPSHOT_DT = (SELECT MAX(SNAPSHOT_DT) FROM dbo.DC_INV) AND (i.MATERIAL_ID LIKE 'FG-100%' OR i.MATERIAL_ID LIKE 'FG-30%') ORDER BY i.MATERIAL_ID, i.DC_ID
SELECT MATERIAL_ID, COUNT(*) n, MAX(SNAPSHOT_DT) mx FROM dbo.DC_INV WHERE MATERIAL_ID LIKE 'FG-3%' GROUP BY MATERIAL_ID

WITH wk AS (SELECT DISTINCT WK_END_DT FROM PHARMA_DEMO.RAW_3P.RXT_WKLY ORDER BY WK_END_DT DESC LIMIT 13),
rx AS (SELECT r.PROD_NDC11, r.PRSCRBR_ME, SUM(r.TRX_QTY) trx FROM PHARMA_DEMO.RAW_3P.RXT_WKLY r JOIN wk ON wk.WK_END_DT=r.WK_END_DT WHERE r.PROD_NDC11 IN ('99101010105','99101010110') GROUP BY 1,2)
SELECT rx.PROD_NDC11, COALESCE(a3.ACCOUNT_ID, a2.ACCOUNT_ID, a1.ACCOUNT_ID) top_acct,
 COALESCE(a3.ACCOUNT_NM, a2.ACCOUNT_NM, a1.ACCOUNT_NM) top_nm, MAX(CASE WHEN a3.PARENT_ACCOUNT_ID IS NOT NULL THEN 'DEEPER' END) deeper,
 SUM(rx.trx) trx13
FROM rx JOIN PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.PRESCRIBER p ON p.PRSCRBR_ME=rx.PRSCRBR_ME
JOIN PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.ACCOUNT a1 ON a1.ACCOUNT_ID=p.ACCOUNT_ID
LEFT JOIN PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.ACCOUNT a2 ON a2.ACCOUNT_ID=a1.PARENT_ACCOUNT_ID
LEFT JOIN PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.ACCOUNT a3 ON a3.ACCOUNT_ID=a2.PARENT_ACCOUNT_ID
WHERE a1.STATE IN ('NY','NJ','PA','MA','FL','GA','NC','OH')
GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 1, trx13 DESC

SELECT s.WHSLR_ID, w.*, SUM(s.UNITS) units_90d FROM dbo.WHSLR_SHIP s JOIN dbo.WHSLR w ON w.WHSLR_ID=s.WHSLR_ID WHERE s.DC_ID='DC-EAST' AND s.MATERIAL_ID IN ('FG-1001','FG-1002') AND s.SHIP_DT >= '2026-07-01' GROUP BY s.WHSLR_ID, w.WHSLR_ID, w.WHSLR_NM

approvals.summary: S-104 (Delmar Specialty Chemicals) will miss PO005791 (RM-221 Polysorbate 80 low-peroxide, 4,200, promised ship 2026-10-07). RM-221 is single-source (S-131 not qualified/not approved in portal) -> no alternate. Feeds Lacrivia 5 mL (FG-1001), Lacrivia 10 mL (FG-1002), Cyclosporine OS 0.05% (FG-1003). Only DC-EAST is below safety stock (snapshot 2026-09-25): FG-1001 46 on hand vs SS 471; FG-1002 34 vs SS 233. Plan per BR-ALLOC-01/02 (Tier A first, pro rata by last-13-week TRx of the NDC from DC-EAST-state prescribers, rounded down, remainder to largest): NDC 99101010105 (46 u x $420 = $19,320): AC00059 Riverbend 20, AC00038 Oak Hollow 15, AC00117 Northfield 11. NDC 99101010110 (34 u x $780 = $26,520): AC00059 15, AC00038 11, AC00117 8. Tier B and other accounts receive none (on-hand exhausted in Tier A). Total 80 units, $45,840 at list -> over $25k threshold (BR-APPR-01). No inter-DC transfer. Recovery: >= 50 days after RM-221 actually ships (earliest 2026-11-26 if it had shipped 10-07). No company substitute: both Lacrivia packs below SS at DC-EAST and Cyclosporine OS is fed by RM-221 (BR-SUB-01/02).

Under the contract-tier allocation rules (approval APR-19080A49), all DC-EAST stock went to Tier A contract accounts, so this account gets no allocation for now. Expected recovery: at least 50 days after the material ships, so not before late November 2026 (2026-11-26 at the earliest). No company substitute is available: Cyclosporine OS 0.05% uses the same material. Medical Affairs will advise on therapeutic alternatives.

escalation_cases.subject: Notify wholesalers W-01 and W-02: Lacrivia supply delay out of DC-EAST
escalation_cases.details: Process step SDR-4.2. The EDI gateway has no API, so this is handed to Trade Relations. Please tell Keystone Drug Distributors (W-01) and Atlas Pharma Supply (W-02), the wholesalers that DC-EAST ships Lacrivia to, about a supply delay. Cause: supplier S-104 (Delmar Specialty Chemicals) will miss the 2026-10-07 ship date for PO005791 (RM-221, Polysorbate 80). Affected at DC-EAST: Lacrivia 0.1% 5 mL (NDC 99101-0101-05 / 99101010105; 46 on hand vs safety stock 471) and Lacrivia 0.1% 10 mL (NDC 99101-0101-10 / 99101010110; 34 on hand vs safety stock 233). The remaining DC-EAST stock is allocated to Tier A contract health systems (allocations AL-0140CB7B and AL-47FBF1BF, approval APR-19080A49). Expected recovery at the DC is at least 50 days after RM-221 ships, so not before 2026-11-26. No company substitute: Cyclosporine OS 0.05% uses the same material. DC-CENTRAL and DC-WEST are above safety stock.

escalation_cases.subject: S-104 RM-221 delay also feeds 11 lens-care finished goods with no governed inventory or demand data
escalation_cases.details: trace_supply_exposure (S-104, RM-221) shows RM-221 (Polysorbate 80 NF, low-peroxide) also feeds 11 lens-care finished goods, FG-3001 to FG-3011 (NDCs 99101-4001-91 to 99101-4011-15), through INT-LC1011/INT-LC2002 at BOM depth 7. These products have no rows in dbo.DC_INV and are not in the commercial database, so the Supply Disruption Response process can't check them against safety stock or allocate them. RM-221 is single-source: S-131 is not qualified and not approved in the supplier portal. Please have the lens-care planners check exposure and stock for these products. Also: S-104 has two more open POs, PO000369 (RM-221, 3,300, promised 2026-10-29) and PO000430 (RM-222, 2,600, promised 2026-10-26). RM-222 has a qualified alternate, S-130 (Oakridge Chemicals), which is active and approved for PL-02, if S-104's delay spreads. Supplier qualification for a second RM-221 source is also recommended, and so is the single-source CMP-310 (S-201).
